# Lite requirements document — Repository usage documentation

Rewrite the kit-scratch README so it says what the repository is for, lists its evidence
branches and pull requests, and states the kit version it was last exercised against.
Today nobody opening kit-scratch can learn any of that without reading the ai-delivery-kit
repository's runbooks.

**Date:** 2026-09-12
**Author:** Generated by the shape skill from Max's guided-interview answers
**Profile:** software (of config: software)
**Entry point:** interview
**Status:** approved (2026-09-12)
**Decomposition:** populated (2026-09-12)
**Notes:** UX ideation skipped: not UI-facing (config records `ui_facing: false`). This
repository file is the requirements home; no Notion copy is published, per the standing
decision in `.ai-delivery/conventions.md` that the repository owns every document. Every
intake question and answer is in `qa-log.md` in this directory, and the Linear project and
issue references are in `tracker.md`.

---

## 1. Problem & Context

**What problem does this solve?**
kit-scratch has no usage documentation. Its README is a two-line note that calls it a
scratch repository and names an old kit version, so anyone opening it cannot tell what it
is for, which branches are evidence, or how the ai-delivery kit is exercised in it. Anyone
given the kit who opens this repository as a worked example meets that gap first.

**Who is affected?**
- Kit maintainer (Max): has to reconstruct the repository's purpose and branch history
  from the ai-delivery-kit runbooks, and signs off on this document.
- First external recipient of the ai-delivery kit: opens kit-scratch to see a worked
  example and cannot make sense of it without the kit repository's runbooks.

**What exists today?**
A two-line README that calls kit-scratch a scratch repository and names an outdated kit
version. To learn what the repository is for, which branches are evidence and why they
stay unmerged, a reader has to read the runbooks in the ai-delivery-kit repository. No
other team is affected: the repository is a fixture, not a product.

---

## 2. Scope

**In Scope:**
- A rewritten README.md that opens with a purpose statement: what kit-scratch is for, and
  that it is a fixture rather than a product.
- A table in README.md of the evidence branches and their pull requests, one line each,
  saying which runbook created each branch and why it stays unmerged.
- A statement in README.md of the kit version the repository was last exercised against,
  naming the ai-delivery-kit repository as where the kit's own records are.

**Out of Scope:**
- Any change to the `.ai-delivery` directory as part of the README work.
  [ASSUMPTION: this document, its Q&A log and the tracker file that the shape skill writes
  under `.ai-delivery/features/` are the kit's working record for this feature, not part
  of the deliverable, so they do not breach this exclusion.]
- Any edit to the evidence branches or their pull requests.
- Any documentation beyond the single README.md.
- Any automation that regenerates the README.

---

## 3. Units of Work

- **Unit 1 (Urgent):** Explain what kit-scratch is for in the README. A first-time reader,
  including the first external recipient of the kit, learns from the README alone that the
  repository is a fixture for exercising the ai-delivery kit and not a product.
- **Unit 2 (Urgent):** List the evidence branches and their pull requests in the README. A
  reader can find any evidence branch and see which runbook created it and why it stays
  unmerged, without opening the ai-delivery-kit repository.
- **Unit 3 (High):** State the kit version kit-scratch was last exercised against. A
  reader knows which kit version the repository reflects and that the kit's own records
  for it are in the ai-delivery-kit repository.

**Happy path:** Open kit-scratch → read the purpose statement → find a branch in the
evidence table → read the kit version and where its records are → Done

---

## 4. Requirements

IDs FR-001 to FR-003 number the functional requirements; each maps to the unit of the same
number above.

| ID | Description | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|----|-------------|----------|---------------------|
| FR-001 | README.md opens with a purpose statement saying kit-scratch is a fixture for exercising the ai-delivery kit, not a product. | Urgent | The first paragraph names the ai-delivery kit, says the repository is a fixture and not a product, and says what it is used for. A reader who has never seen the kit repository can state the repository's purpose from that paragraph alone. The old two-line note and its outdated kit version no longer appear. |
| FR-002 | README.md contains a table of the evidence branches and their pull requests, one row per branch. | Urgent | Each evidence branch in the repository's branch list has exactly one row. [ASSUMPTION: every branch other than `main` is an evidence branch.] Each row gives the branch name, its pull request number (or "none" when it has no open pull request), the runbook that created it, and one line on why it stays unmerged. Branch names and pull request numbers match the repository's branch list and its open pull requests on GitHub as of the date stated above the table. |
| FR-003 | README.md states the kit version the repository was last exercised against and names the ai-delivery-kit repository as where the kit's own records are. | High | The README states exactly one kit version number as the version last exercised. It names the ai-delivery-kit repository by name only, with no link to any individual runbook. |

**Design-system components:** Not applicable. This feature is not UI-facing.

**Key constraints:**
- Sources: branch names come from the repository's own branch list, and pull requests from
  its open pull requests on GitHub, never from the kit's ledgers. [ASSUMPTION: the
  creating runbook and the reason a branch stays unmerged are read from that branch's pull
  request description or commit messages.]
- Format: plain Markdown, plain tone, no em dashes, and the whole README fits on one
  screen. [ASSUMPTION: one screen means at most 40 lines of Markdown source.]
- References: the ai-delivery-kit repository is named, not linked, and no individual
  runbook is linked.
- Freshness: nothing regenerates the README, so the evidence table is a dated snapshot and
  states the date its facts were read.
- Delivery: no evidence branch or its pull request is touched. [ASSUMPTION: the README
  change is delivered on its own new branch.]
